hints.content: The arrow points to all values greater than $1$.
And the point at $1$ is filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything **greater than or equal to $1$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**


[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at 1 and continues right. A closed point is plotted at 1 where the line begins.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x < 1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at 1 and continues left. An open point is plotted at 1 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/a0b660aebcdd7379d0039482676b33e68aebe734)

The graph of $x \leq 1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at 1 and continues left. A closed point is plotted at 1 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/3599ae1eb9d2f6a33349977cfe525420e176c72c)

The graph of $x >1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at 1 and continues right. An open point is plotted at 1 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/e2e68f2c3f070ef8ff816038db2684ccb8c506d6)
